name: EPA ECHO sewer overflow and bypass event reports (eRule Phase 2, NeT-SewerOverflow), SD rows
operator: US EPA (ECHO); reports filed by permittees through NeT-SewerOverflow
waters_covered: statewide; receiving water free text in a child table (often blank)
access_detail: Daily ZIP from ECHO; table sewer_overflow_bypass_report_events.csv joined to sewer_overflow_bypass_receiving_waters.csv on sewer_overflow_bypass_event_key; filter permit_identifier prefix. Pipeline already has pipeline/ingest/echo_sewer_overflow_events.py. Trimmed sample in raw/sobe-sample.json.

sample_record.sewer_overflow_reporting_requirement_des: 5-day reporting for noncompliance that may endanger health or the environment

cadence: Extract rebuilt daily; these are the 5-day written reports, so they appear days to weeks after the event (start-to-receipt median 5 days; 10% same day, 10% over 48 days).
history: Rows from April 2023 (NeT pilot) to date
license: EPA public data; no restriction stated
legal_basis: 40 CFR 127 (NPDES eRule Phase 2, from 2025-12-21); 40 CFR 122.41(l)(6) five-day written report
status_reason: The only dated, statewide, machine-readable overflow feed for South Dakota, read by the national eRule ingester (echo-sewer-overflow) with South Dakota in its states. 2026-11-04 extract: 208 current SD rows from 56 permits (SSO 167, BYP 40, CSO 1), starts 2023-04-20 to 2026-11-02; every row with a point, 186 with a volume, 74 with a receiving-water row. 56 kept from 30 permits; 152 dropped (97 SSOs naming no water and no water impact, 34 building backups, 21 naming no water in words). Received a median 5 days after the start (10% the same day, 10% 57 days or more). Times read in the zone of the event's own point (Mountain in the fifteen counties 49 CFR 71.7(b) puts west of the boundary: 70 rows; Central elsewhere: 138).

name: SD DANR spill reports (NR42 Interactive Map, Tanks and Spills database)
operator: South Dakota Department of Agriculture and Natural Resources
access_detail: Map at apps.sd.gov/NR42InteractiveMap (200); ArcGIS MapServer arcgis.sd.gov/arcgis/rest/services/DENR/NR42_SpillReports_Public reset the connection to curl and returned 503 to WebFetch. Column definitions PDF fetched: danr.sd.gov/Agriculture/Inspection/Spills/docs/Tanks_and_Spills_Map_Spill_download_columns_defined.pdf.
legal_basis: SDCL 34A-12; ARSD 74:34:01:05 ('Suspected Discharges must be reported to DANR within 24 Hours')
status_reason: A remediation case list (case number, status, dates reported and closed, site, lat/long, material, amount, spill category PETROLEUM/CHEMICAL/AGRI CHEM/OIL/COMBINED/OTHER). The reporting page covers petroleum and chemicals and does not mention sewage; municipal overflows go through the permit route (SOBE), so this is not an SSO source.
notes: Responsible-party and reviewer columns would need stripping.

name: SD DANR 2026 Shoreline Microcystin Samples (ArcGIS)
operator: South Dakota DANR, Water Protection Program
status_reason: Public layer, 21 lake stations in 2026, wide format (Date_1..Date_5, Microcystin_1..5); e.g. Clear Lake 14.405 on 08/18/2026. One new service per year.

name: SD DANR HABs Advisories layers (yearly) and HAB web page
access_detail: https://services1.arcgis.com/PwrabBhZHUggYYSp/arcgis/rest/services/2024_HABs_Advisories_view/FeatureServer/0 (fields Number, Waterbody, Date, Reason, Latitude, Longitude). Web map e35e4698ef6c43669c6fb7d1c6b163da.
cadence: the page's list changes when DANR issues an advisory; read every run
status_reason: DANR's HAB page now opens with a box "Harmful Algal Bloom Advisories 2026" listing each lake under advisory with its county and a date (five lakes on 2026-11-07: Twin Lakes, Spink County, 6/15/2026; Wall Lake, Minnehaha County, 8/11/2026; Clear Lake, Hamlin County, 8/18/2026; Lake Poinsett, Hamlin County, 9/15/2026; Lake Albert, Kingsbury County, 9/15/2026); "Advisories expire at the end of the calendar year". Read by the sd-danr-hab-advisories ingester. The yearly advisory map layers stop at 2024 (2024: 3 rows, e.g. Brant Lake, microcystin 9.46 above 8 ug/L), and DANR warns its map 'does not show current conditions'.
